title: Wendelin: faith not simple virtue — knowledge, assent, trust span powers
source_text: XIV. Eodem quoque argumento utitur Wendelinus, ut probet, fidem non in solo haerere intellectu, sed ad voluntatem quoque pertinere. Theol. Christ. lib. 1. cap. 24. in explicatione 1. theses cretavae. Ubi etiam observat fidem non esse virtutem simplicem; sed diversis constare partibus, notitia, assensu & fiducia, quae ad eandem potentiam non pertinent.
pass_a_gloss: Wendelin uses the same argument to prove faith does not cling in intellect alone but also belongs to the will (Theol. Christ. 1.24, in explaining the first Cretan thesis). There he also observes that faith is not a simple virtue but consists of diverse parts — knowledge, assent, and trust — which do not belong to the same power.
pass_b_english: Wendelin: same will-argument; faith is not a simple virtue.
Parts (knowledge, assent, trust) do not all belong to one power.
